title: Frontend bundle slimming and targeted subtle motion

requirements.summary: Measure and record baseline production JS payload, then reduce shipped JS by ~90% while keeping core flows working.
acceptanceCriteria: A baseline production build size (JS payload) is measured and recorded before changes.

After optimizations, the production JS payload is reduced by ~90% versus the recorded baseline (or the closest achievable reduction is documented with a clear breakdown of remaining largest contributors).
The app continues to function as before (no broken navigation or core workflows).

file_operations.description: Add a lightweight, repo-tracked bundle size report template with sections for baseline measurement, post-change measurement, and a table of largest JS contributors (record actual values during implementation).

Introduce route/view-level code splitting using React.lazy/Suspense so non-initial views (e.g., Vault/Builder/Preview/Rules/Settings/Rarity/Workshop as appropriate) are loaded on demand; keep Dashboard and project editing flow functional.
Create a tiny local icon set (inline SVG React components) to replace heavy icon dependencies across the app, focusing on the most frequently used icons first (navigation, modal controls, toolbars).
Replace lucide-react icon imports with local inline SVG icons to reduce shipped JS, preserving the existing header behavior and navigation.
Replace lucide-react Heart icon with a local inline SVG icon to reduce shipped JS while preserving the footer layout and link behavior.

requirements.summary: Optimize bundle size by removing/replacing heavy dependencies, deleting unused code, and ensuring large features are lazy-loaded (without adding animation libraries).
acceptanceCriteria: No new animation libraries (e.g., Lottie, Framer Motion) are added.
Large non-critical UI routes/components are loaded via code-splitting (lazy loading) when it meaningfully reduces initial bundle size.
No runtime errors are introduced in the browser console during typical use.

file_operations.description: Reduce dependency weight by replacing lucide-react imports with local inline SVG icons, and ensure any browser-incompatible typings are removed (keep behavior unchanged).
Replace lucide-react icon imports with local inline SVG icons (and keep existing validations and user-facing English text unchanged) to reduce shipped JS.
Replace lucide-react icon imports with local inline SVG icons and keep modal/rule workflows intact; avoid adding any new animation dependencies.
Replace lucide-react icon usage (if present) with local inline SVG icons and remove any dead/unused imports to reduce shipped JS while keeping dashboard interactions intact.
Replace lucide-react icon usage (if present) with local inline SVG icons and eliminate unused imports/logic to reduce shipped JS without changing publishing workflow behavior.

requirements.summary: Add subtle, performance-friendly motion to selected components (buttons, modals, and at least one icon-button set) using Tailwind/CSS/React only.
acceptanceCriteria: Buttons provide immediate visual press feedback (e.g., subtle scale/translate and transition) and consistent hover/focus transitions.
Modals animate in/out with a subtle slide+scale and a softened backdrop effect, without jarring motion.
At least one set of commonly used icon buttons uses lightweight animated SVG/CSS (no external animation libraries) to convey interactivity.

file_operations.description: Remove global motion/animation rules that apply to all buttons/links and all Radix dialog overlays/contents; instead add scoped utility classes for subtle motion (e.g., .motion-button, .motion-icon-button, .motion-modal-overlay, .motion-modal-content) and ensure prefers-reduced-motion remains respected.

Create a small wrapper component for icon buttons that applies subtle hover/press/focus motion via className composition (no new animation libraries), to be used on selected icon buttons (e.g., close/menu actions).

Apply the new scoped modal motion classes to the Dialog overlay/content via className composition, and apply scoped motion classes to the primary action Button to provide subtle press feedback (do not modify any files under frontend/src/components/ui; compose instead).

Apply the new scoped modal motion classes to dialog overlay/content and apply scoped motion classes to action buttons for subtle hover/press feedback (compose shadcn components; do not modify frontend/src/components/ui).
Apply scoped modal motion classes for in/out animation and softened backdrop, and ensure the Cancel/Delete buttons have consistent subtle hover/press/focus transitions without making motion global.

Use the new MotionIconButton (or equivalent scoped motion classes) for the mobile menu icon button and ensure the icon itself has a lightweight CSS/SVG interactive animation (e.g., subtle rotate/scale on hover/press) without introducing third-party animation libraries.

Apply scoped modal motion classes to the NFT detail modal overlay/content and use MotionIconButton (or scoped motion classes) for the close icon button to satisfy icon-button motion requirement while keeping performance-friendly transitions.

requirements.summary: Fix the prior build failure risk and ensure the frontend builds successfully (development and production) after the changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend canister compilation succeeds without errors.
The deployed app loads and the main pages render and function (Dashboard and project editing flows).

file_operations.description: Remove browser-incompatible Node.js typings (e.g., replace NodeJS.Timeout with ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> where used) and verify the worker creation and modal logic still compiles and runs in production builds.
Ensure Suspense fallback/loading states are present for lazy-loaded views so navigation remains functional and production builds compile without missing imports.
Ensure icons are exported with stable names/props so all updated imports compile cleanly; keep the icon module dependency-free to avoid build regressions.
Record any build issues encountered/fixed during implementation and document the final build verification checklist for dev and production builds (frontend focus).
